113.title: Meet Major Vivek Singh Bhandral: 21 Para SF Officer Who Killed Two Terrorists Despite Being Gravely Wounded
body: On 29 August 2002, deep inside the forests of the Machhal sector in Kupwara, a search party of 21 Para (Special Forces) was closing in on a militant hideout when the operation suddenly turned into a close-quarter firefight. Two terrorists burst out of a house and opened fire on the troops. Within moments, the leading scout and the squad commander were wounded. Major Vivek Singh Bhandral took the fight forward. He killed one terrorist at close range, pursued the second into a nearby grove and continued the assault even after being struck by a burst of machine-gun fire. 186.title: Army, BSF Hold Synergy Seminar in Shillong to Boost Border Coordination

The "Army-BSF Synergy Seminar 2026" was hosted by the 101 Area of the Army's Eastern Command. Participants included senior officers from the BSF's Meghalaya, Guwahati, Mizoram, and Cachar and Tripura Frontiers. The BSF is in charge of managing the 4,096 km border with Bangladesh. Of this, 856 km lies in Tripura, 443 km in Meghalaya, 318 km in Mizoram, and 262 km in Assam. The remaining 2,217 km of the border is managed by the South Bengal and North Bengal Frontiers of West Bengal. The terrain through which the border runs makes management difficult. It comprises riverine, forested, and hilly stretches, where fencing is difficult.

138.title: Assam Rifles: India's Only Paramilitary Force
body: The Assam Rifles is one of the most distinctive forces in India's security architecture — and one of the least understood. Its origins go back to 1835, when it was raised as the Cachar Levy with just 750 men. Created to protect British interests and settlements in the Northeast, the force went through several transformations — Assam Frontier Police, Assam Military Police and Eastern Bengal and Assam Military Police — before taking its present name in 1917. Nearly two centuries later, the Assam Rifles remains deeply embedded in the security landscape of the Northeast. Unlike the Central Armed Police Forces — CRPF, BSF, CISF, ITBP and SSB — the Assam Rifles has a distinctive Army-linked command structure. Its administrative affairs fall under the Ministry of Home Affairs, while its operational command is exercised through the Army.

157.title: Foreign Nationals: A New Security Question for India
body: The challenge before India in Manipur is manifold; there is a weapons smuggling racket, high ethnic tensions and freely narcotics available. The usual route for narco-traffickers is China-Myanmar and then to India's North-East. Myanmar is also the provider of substantial quantities of arms and ammunition, which is being smuggled into India. In September 2026, the police in Manipur recovered a haul of 328 illegal arms including AK-47s, and INSAS rifles with substantial amounts of ammunition. However, a different security challenge has emerged in recent years: the growing presence of foreign nationals allegedly involved in the movement and smuggling of drones into Myanmar and Bangladesh, posing a new concern for Indian security planners. Some of them are private military contractors with an American background, while many act on behalf of criminal groups, which engage in transnational narco-terrorism.
